Objects: Write R_+=[0,infinity), and let lambda_T be Lebesgue measure on [0,T], transported to R_+ (the given comap of volume restricted to [0,T]). All time integrals below use this measure unless indicated otherwise. For n in N put t[n,i]=i*T/2^n for i=0,...,2^n, and Delta_i^n Z=Z(t[n,i+1])-Z(t[n,i]). A ProgressiveL2Integrand eta on horizon T is a real process eta(t,omega), strongly progressive for the filtration, with (omega,t) -> eta(t,omega) in L^2(mu x lambda_T). I_T^j(eta) denotes the supplied completed continuous Ito process driven by the scalar coordinate B_j(t,omega)=(B(t,omega))_j: the pointwise limit of chosen elementary stochastic-integral approximations off their null uniform-Cauchy bad set, zero on that bad set, and held constant after T; at each t<=T it agrees almost everywhere with the L^2-completion integral up to t. Define R(t,omega)=sum_j I_T^j(eta_j)(min(tau(omega),t),omega). Define e_n(omega)=sum_i (Delta_i^n R(omega))^2-sum_j integral_{s<=tau(omega)} eta_j(s,omega)^2 d lambda_T(s). The integrand's toLp operation is its L^2 equivalence class represented by (omega,t)->eta(t,omega).

Domains: Omega measurable; J finite with decidable equality; mu finite; filtration on R_+; T>0; vector Brownian B in R^J; eta:J->ProgressiveL2Integrand(filtration,mu,T); tau:Omega->R_+.

Quantifiers: Universally spaces,filtration,mu,T,B; Brownian,positive-T,usual assumptions; eta,tau; stopping-time and bound assumptions. Conclusion first forall n, then the limit as n->infinity.

Assumptions: The vector Brownian hypothesis means B(0,omega)=0 for every omega; increments on finite families of pairwise disjoint half-open intervals are jointly independent; every continuous real linear functional ell sends B(t)-B(s), s<t, to a centered Gaussian of variance (t-s)||ell||^2; paths are mu-almost surely continuous. B is strongly adapted, and for every s<=t the increment B(t)-B(s) is independent of the sigma-algebra filtration(s). The filtration is right continuous, and every mu-null subset of Omega belongs to filtration(t) for every t>=0 (completeness at each time). The coercion omega->tau(omega) into extended nonnegative reals is a stopping time for the filtration (the supplied IsChewiStoppingTime is exactly IsStoppingTime); tau(omega)<=T for every omega.

Conclusion: Every e_n is mu-integrable, and integral_Omega |e_n(omega)|dmu tends to zero as n->infinity.

Scopes: This is L^1 convergence of the stopped quadratic-variation error to zero. The stopping-time bound is pointwise, not only almost sure. Integrals restrict to s<=tau(omega); the partition remains the deterministic dyadic partition of [0,T].

Constant dependencies: No bound or rate constant is stated. e_n depends on T,tau,eta and the completed Ito processes; convergence may depend on all input data.
